card.statement:
Let $G$ be an affine group scheme over $\mathbf{k}$. Then $G$ is algebraic if and only if there exists $X\in{\mathord{\mathrm{Rep}}}_{\mathbf{k}}(G)$ such that $X$ generates ${\mathord{\mathrm{Rep}}}_{\mathbf{k}}(G)$ by taking direct sums, tensor products, duals, and subquotients.

Let $G$ be an algebraic affine group scheme over $\mathbf{k}$. If $G$ is not connected, then there exists a nontrivial representation $X\in{\mathord{\mathrm{Rep}}}_{\mathbf{k}}(G)$ such that the subcategory $\langle X\rangle$ (with the notation of §2.1) is stable under $\otimes$.

Let $G$ be a connected algebraic affine group scheme over $\mathbf{k}$. Assume that $\mathbf{k}$ has characteristic $0$, and that ${\mathord{\mathrm{Rep}}}_{\overline{\mathbf{k}}}(G_{\overline{\mathbf{k}}})$ is semisimple, where $\overline{\mathbf{k}}$ is an algebraic closure of $\mathbf{k}$ and $G_{\overline{\mathbf{k}}}=\mathrm{Spec}(\overline{\mathbf{k}})\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbf{k})}G$. Then $G$ is reductive.
card.label: Proposition 2.11

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
